description.describe_ch: 課程內容著重培養媒體識讀能力，教導學生如何識別偏見、假資訊，並能批判性地解讀資訊。學生將學習如何運用事實查核工具，並分析媒體如何影響公眾輿論，課程內容也會探討影響資訊傳播的各項因素。
description.describe_eh: The course emphasizes media literacy by teaching students how to identify bias, recognize misinformation, and critically analyze information. Students will gain hands-on experience using fact-checking tools and analyzing the role of media in shaping public opinion. They will also explore factors influencing the spread of information.

targets.describe_en: Critically evaluate information and its sources.

targets.describe_ch: 能呈現對資訊的觀察與解讀。
targets.describe_en: Present their observation and interpretation of information.

readings.tpc_book_en:

  • Download the AP News APP | AP News

weeklyScds.tpd_learn_en: A primer on the history, development and current streams of conservative thought in the western idiom. HW: Readings.
A primer on the history and development of liberal thought and its transformation into the "left" and its current streams of thought in the western idiom. HW: Readings.

An intro to news media, its sections, its genres, and its stylistic conventions (5Ws and an H). Then students will be instructed into how to use the news aggregate site: SmartNews. Other news aggregate sites will be introduced that they can also use. They will select and explore.

Kahoot quiz on readings from weeks 2 and 3.
In pairs and with teacher guidance students choose a recent news story. Analyze how different outlets report the story, noting any differences in language, emphasis, and framing - especially with regard to the left and right. They write a one to three sentence summary. They then do a breakdown of it using the 5W and an H method. They then summarize the main points. These summaries will be uploaded into their upload folders to create a portfolio.
Students, having chosen one of the above stories, present their findings to the class, highlighting how media bias can influence perception.
An exploration of evidence of biases in social media reportage. HW: Readings

Understanding the role of social media is critical for analyzing how news is spread and consumed in today's digital world. A primer on the influence of algorithms, echo chambers and polarization and misinformation and virality. HW: Critical Engagement Activity: Students track a trending news story on different social media platforms over a week. They should analyze how the story evolves, what types of content get the most engagement, and how different perspectives are presented or omitted.

Roundtable discussion: how did the story evolve, what types of contents got the most engagement, and how were different perspectives presented or omitted? Each group presents their findings that are opened up to a group discussion

Quiz on material covered from weeks 8-11.
An introduction to news media podcasts w/ analysis and examples. HW: Create a podcast for this week’s news.

Quiz on material covered from weeks 8-11.
An introduction to news media podcasts w/ analysis and examples. HW: Create a podcast for this week’s news.
Students present their news podcast to the class.

Students write a one to three sentence summary of an article of their choice. They then do a breakdown of it using the 5W and an H method. They then summarize the main points. Summaries added to portfolio.

Students write a one to three sentence summary of an article of their choice. They then do a breakdown of it using the 5W and an H method. They then summarize the main points. Summaries added to portfolio.
Students create groups and prepare for their final presentations – seeking teacher feedback.
The Newsroom. Groups will present a news show with stories from a minimum of 5 categories.

gradeRuleDescribe.tpa_score_new_en:
1. Attendance and Punctuality
- Regular Attendance: Students are expected to attend all classes, including seminars, group discussions, and presentations. Attendance will be recorded, and excessive absences may impact your participation grade.
- Punctuality: Please arrive on time for each class. If you are late, enter quietly and do not disrupt the ongoing discussion or activity. Repeated tardiness may result in a deduction of participation points.
 
 2. Participation and Engagement
- Active Engagement: Participation in discussions and group work is a key component of this course. Students should come prepared, having read assigned materials and ready to contribute thoughtfully to class discussions.
- Respectful Communication: All students are expected to engage in discussions respectfully, even when there are differences in opinion. Listen actively, and address others’ viewpoints with openness and courtesy.
- Language Use: As this course is conducted in English, students are encouraged to speak in English during all class activities. Mistakes are part of the learning process—focus on communicating your ideas clearly rather than perfectly.
 
 3. Group Work and Collaboration
- Teamwork Etiquette: Group work requires cooperation, and all members are expected to contribute equally. Respect each other’s perspectives, distribute tasks fairly, and support each other in achieving group objectives.
- Accountability: If a group member is not contributing or is causing difficulties, address the issue within the group first. If the problem persists, inform the instructor so that it can be resolved.
- Group Assignments: Each group is responsible for meeting deadlines and submitting collaborative assignments on time. Late submissions will affect the group's grade unless prior arrangements have been made with the instructor.
 
 4. Presentations
- Preparation: All presentations must be well-prepared and rehearsed. Make sure that your presentation is clear, organized, and relevant to the assigned topic.
- Engagement with Audience: Encourage interaction during your presentation by posing questions or inviting comments. Your aim should be to facilitate discussion, not just to deliver information.
- Respect for Presenters: When your peers are presenting, be attentive and respectful. Save questions or comments for the designated discussion time and refrain from talking or using devices during presentations.
 
 5. Academic Integrity
- Plagiarism: All submitted work must be your own. Plagiarism, including copying from other students or sources without proper citation, will result in academic penalties.
- Source Attribution: When using information from news articles, podcasts, or other sources, make sure to properly cite these references both in written assignments and presentations.
- Integrity in Group Work: While collaboration is encouraged, ensure that your contributions are original and that you give credit to all group members' ideas.
 
 6. Technology Use
- Devices in Class: Laptops and tablets can be used for note-taking and research during class activities. However, please avoid using your devices for non-academic purposes during class time.
 
 7. Assignment Submission and Deadlines
- Submission Policy: All assignments and reading journals must be submitted by the specified deadline. Late submissions will incur a grade reduction unless you have communicated with the instructor in advance.
- Extensions: If you are unable to meet a deadline due to valid reasons, request an extension before the due date. Extensions will be granted at the instructor's discretion.
 
 8. Classroom Conduct
- Mutual Respect: Respect the opinions and ideas of your classmates, especially during sensitive discussions on politics, media bias, or cultural differences. Avoid personal attacks or inflammatory language.
 
 9. Communication with Instructor
- Office Hours: Take advantage of the instructor's office hours for questions or concerns about the course material, assignments, or group dynamics.
- Email Etiquette: When emailing the instructor, use a polite and professional tone. Include your full name, the course title, and a brief description of your query.
 
 10. Grading and Evaluation
- Participation Grade: Your participation will be graded based on your contributions to class discussions, group work, and your engagement with the course materials.

gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno:
At Feng-Chia University, we are committed to upholding the highest standards of academic integrity. We believe that honesty, trust, and ethical conduct are fundamental to the pursuit of knowledge, the advancement of learning, and the educational mission of our institution.
 
As members of the academic community, students, faculty, and staff are expected to adhere to the following principles of academic integrity:
 
1. Honesty: All academic work should be the result of individual effort and original thought. Plagiarism, cheating, and any form of dishonesty are unacceptable and will not be tolerated.
 
2. Attribution: Proper citation and acknowledgment of sources are essential when using the ideas, words, or creations of others. Failure to provide appropriate attribution constitutes plagiarism.
 
3. Collaboration: Collaboration among students on assignments or projects is permissible when explicitly authorized by the instructor. However, in all cases, the individual contribution of each student should be clearly indicated.
 
4. Examination Integrity: During examinations, students are expected to abide by the rules and guidelines established by the instructor. Any form of cheating or unauthorized assistance is strictly prohibited.
 
5. Respect for Intellectual Property: Unauthorized distribution, reproduction, or sharing of copyrighted materials is a violation of academic integrity and may also infringe upon legal rights.
 
6. Falsification of Information: Providing false information or documents to gain academic advantage, such as falsifying research data or doctoring transcripts, is a serious breach of integrity.
 
7. Adherence to Course Policies: Students should familiarize themselves with the specific course policies and expectations outlined in the syllabus provided by the instructor.
 
8. Reporting Violations: It is the responsibility of all members of the academic community to report suspected violations of academic integrity. Reports can be made to the instructor, academic advisors, or other appropriate university officials.
 
Violations of academic integrity will be thoroughly investigated, and appropriate sanctions will be applied in accordance with institutional policies. These sanctions may include, but are not limited to, failing grades on assignments or exams, course failure, suspension, or expulsion from the institution.
 
We believe that academic integrity is a shared responsibility and that maintaining these principles is essential to the credibility and reputation of our institution. By adhering to these standards, we ensure the fairness and integrity of our educational environment and promote the development of ethical individuals who are well-prepared to contribute to society.
 
Feng-Chia University expects all members of its community to uphold these principles and demonstrate a commitment to academic integrity in all academic pursuits.

- Language Use: As this course is conducted in English, students are encouraged to speak in English during all class activities. Mistakes are part of the learning process—focus on communicating your ideas clearly rather than perfectly.

 3. Group Work and Collaboration
- Teamwork Etiquette: Group work requires cooperation, and all members are expected to contribute equally. Respect each other’s perspectives, distribute tasks fairly, and support each other in achieving group objectives.
- Accountability: If a group member is not contributing or is causing difficulties, address the issue within the group first. If the problem persists, inform the instructor so that it can be resolved.
- Group Assignments: Each group is responsible for meeting deadlines and submitting collaborative assignments on time. Late submissions will affect the group's grade unless prior arrangements have been made with the instructor.

 4. Presentations
- Preparation: All presentations must be well-prepared and rehearsed. Make sure that your presentation is clear, organized, and relevant to the assigned topic.
- Engagement with Audience: Encourage interaction during your presentation by posing questions or inviting comments. Your aim should be to facilitate discussion, not just to deliver information.
- Respect for Presenters: When your peers are presenting, be attentive and respectful. Save questions or comments for the designated discussion time and refrain from talking or using devices during presentations.

 5. Academic Integrity
- Plagiarism: All submitted work must be your own. Plagiarism, including copying from other students or sources without proper citation, will result in academic penalties.
- Source Attribution: When using information from news articles, podcasts, or other sources, make sure to properly cite these references both in written assignments and presentations.
- Integrity in Group Work: While collaboration is encouraged, ensure that your contributions are original and that you give credit to all group members' ideas.

 6. Technology Use
- Devices in Class: Laptops and tablets can be used for note-taking and research during class activities. However, please avoid using your devices for non-academic purposes during class time.

 7. Assignment Submission and Deadlines
- Submission Policy: All assignments and reading journals must be submitted by the specified deadline. Late submissions will incur a grade reduction unless you have communicated with the instructor in advance.
- Extensions: If you are unable to meet a deadline due to valid reasons, request an extension before the due date. Extensions will be granted at the instructor's discretion.

 8. Classroom Conduct
- Mutual Respect: Respect the opinions and ideas of your classmates, especially during sensitive discussions on politics, media bias, or cultural differences. Avoid personal attacks or inflammatory language.

 9. Communication with Instructor
- Office Hours: Take advantage of the instructor's office hours for questions or concerns about the course material, assignments, or group dynamics.
- Email Etiquette: When emailing the instructor, use a polite and professional tone. Include your full name, the course title, and a brief description of your query.

 10. Grading and Evaluation
- Participation Grade: Your participation will be graded based on your contributions to class discussions, group work, and your engagement with the course materials.
policy.ais_meno:
At Feng-Chia University, we are committed to upholding the highest standards of academic integrity. We believe that honesty, trust, and ethical conduct are fundamental to the pursuit of knowledge, the advancement of learning, and the educational mission of our institution.
 
As members of the academic community, students, faculty, and staff are expected to adhere to the following principles of academic integrity:
 
1. Honesty: All academic work should be the result of individual effort and original thought. Plagiarism, cheating, and any form of dishonesty are unacceptable and will not be tolerated.
 
2. Attribution: Proper citation and acknowledgment of sources are essential when using the ideas, words, or creations of others. Failure to provide appropriate attribution constitutes plagiarism.
 
3. Collaboration: Collaboration among students on assignments or projects is permissible when explicitly authorized by the instructor. However, in all cases, the individual contribution of each student should be clearly indicated.
 
4. Examination Integrity: During examinations, students are expected to abide by the rules and guidelines established by the instructor. Any form of cheating or unauthorized assistance is strictly prohibited.
 
5. Respect for Intellectual Property: Unauthorized distribution, reproduction, or sharing of copyrighted materials is a violation of academic integrity and may also infringe upon legal rights.
 
6. Falsification of Information: Providing false information or documents to gain academic advantage, such as falsifying research data or doctoring transcripts, is a serious breach of integrity.
 
7. Adherence to Course Policies: Students should familiarize themselves with the specific course policies and expectations outlined in the syllabus provided by the instructor.
 
8. Reporting Violations: It is the responsibility of all members of the academic community to report suspected violations of academic integrity. Reports can be made to the instructor, academic advisors, or other appropriate university officials.
 
Violations of academic integrity will be thoroughly investigated, and appropriate sanctions will be applied in accordance with institutional policies. These sanctions may include, but are not limited to, failing grades on assignments or exams, course failure, suspension, or expulsion from the institution.
 
We believe that academic integrity is a shared responsibility and that maintaining these principles is essential to the credibility and reputation of our institution. By adhering to these standards, we ensure the fairness and integrity of our educational environment and promote the development of ethical individuals who are well-prepared to contribute to society.
 
Feng-Chia University expects all members of its community to uphold these principles and demonstrate a commitment to academic integrity in all academic pursuits.
